explanation_en: A common collocation meaning to have a significant effect or to make a positive impact. While it translates directly to English, it is a crucial idiomatic pattern in Portuguese where 'fazer' is used instead of other verbs. It is appropriate for all registers, from casual conversation to formal speeches.

examples.en_text: Drinking more water every day really makes a difference for your health.
examples.target_text: Beber mais água todos os dias realmente faz diferença para a saúde.

examples.en_text: The help you gave me yesterday made all the difference.
examples.target_text: A ajuda que você me deu ontem fez toda a diferença.

examples.en_text: To me, it doesn't make a difference if we go by car or by bus.
examples.target_text: Para mim, não faz diferença se vamos de carro ou de ônibus.

examples.en_text: I hope this new course makes a difference in your career.
examples.target_text: Eu espero que este novo curso faça diferença na sua carreira.

examples.en_text: If you studied a bit more, that would make a big difference on the exam.
examples.target_text: Se você estudasse um pouco mais, isso faria muita diferença na prova.

examples.en_text: Small details can make a difference in the final result of the project.
examples.target_text: Pequenos detalhes podem fazer diferença no resultado final do projeto.

explanation_en: Literally meaning 'to turn into a callus,' this expression is used to describe something that becomes a constant source of irritation, a nuisance, or a persistent problem. It is similar to the English idiom 'a thorn in one's side.' It is moderately informal but very expressive.

examples.en_text: That monthly report became a thorn in my side; I spend hours trying to solve it.
examples.target_text: Aquele relatório mensal virou um calo na minha vida; passo horas tentando resolver.

examples.en_text: The new neighbor became a thorn in everyone's side in the building with all that noise.
examples.target_text: O novo vizinho virou um calo no pé de todo mundo no prédio com aquele barulho.

examples.en_text: This old car has already become a nuisance. Every week I have to go to the mechanic.
examples.target_text: Esse carro velho já virou um calo. Toda semana tenho que ir ao mecânico.

examples.en_text: This delivery app became a thorn in the side for restaurants because of the high fees.
examples.target_text: Esse aplicativo de entregas virou um calo para os restaurantes por causa das taxas altas.

examples.en_text: Resolving this problem with the bank became a real nuisance in my routine.
examples.target_text: Resolver esse problema com o banco virou um verdadeiro calo na minha rotina.

examples.en_text: That opponent team always becomes a thorn in our side when we play at their stadium.
examples.target_text: Aquele time adversário sempre vira um calo para nós quando jogamos na casa deles.

explanation_en: This metaphorical expression means to draw resources, ideas, inspiration, or benefits from a specific origin. In political or business contexts, it often implies exploiting a lucrative system or taking advantage of a specific funding stream. It can be used both positively (e.g., learning from a great master) and critically (e.g., exploiting a system).

examples.en_text: If you want to be a good writer, you need to read the classics and drink from that source.
examples.target_text: Se você quer ser um bom escritor, precisa ler os clássicos e beber dessa fonte.

examples.en_text: Many new startups try to draw inspiration from this source to achieve the same success.
examples.target_text: Muitas startups novas tentam beber dessa fonte para alcançar o mesmo sucesso.

examples.en_text: He studied with the best scientists in the country and knew how to benefit from that source of knowledge.
examples.target_text: Ele estudou com os melhores cientistas do país e soube beber dessa fonte.

examples.en_text: The band's new album shows that they continue to draw inspiration from that source of classic rock.
examples.target_text: O novo álbum da banda mostra que eles continuam a beber dessa fonte do rock clássico.

examples.en_text: My grandmother has a lot of wisdom and I always try to drink from that source when I talk to her.
examples.target_text: Minha avó tem muita sabedoria e eu sempre tento beber dessa fonte quando converso com ela.

examples.en_text: The workshop was amazing; all the participants were able to drink from this source of knowledge.
examples.target_text: O workshop foi incrível; todos os participantes puderam beber dessa fonte de conhecimento.

explanation_en: Literally meaning 'to give reason,' this common idiom is used when you acknowledge that someone is correct or justified in their stance. It is followed by the preposition 'a' or 'para' when referring to a person.

examples.en_text: After thinking about the matter carefully, I have to admit he is right.
examples.target_text: Depois de pensar bem no assunto, tenho de lhe dar razão.

examples.en_text: My parents finally admitted I was right about the choice of course.
examples.target_text: Os meus pais finalmente me deram razão sobre a escolha do curso.

examples.en_text: If you listen to his argument carefully, you will agree he is right.
examples.target_text: Se tu ouvires o argumento dele com atenção, vais dar-lhe razão.

examples.en_text: He is very stubborn and never admits anyone else is right.
examples.target_text: Ele é muito teimoso e nunca dá razão a ninguém.

examples.en_text: At the end of the discussion, she ended up agreeing with me.
examples.target_text: No final da discussão, ela acabou por me dar razão.

examples.en_text: I hope the boss agrees we are right this time, because we have data that proves what we are saying.
examples.target_text: Espero que o chefe nos dê razão desta vez, porque temos dados que provam o que dizemos.

explanation_en: A formal collocation meaning to express reservations, objections, or caveats about a statement, person, or idea. It is essential for academic, professional, and analytical discussions in Portuguese.

examples.en_text: I agree with the plan, but I need to make some reservations before signing.
examples.target_text: Eu concordo com o plano, mas preciso fazer algumas ressalvas antes de assinar.

examples.en_text: If you accept the proposal, make reservations about the delivery deadline.
examples.target_text: Caso você aceite a proposta, faça ressalvas sobre o prazo de entrega.

examples.en_text: The director approved the project, but made reservations regarding the final budget.
examples.target_text: O diretor aprovou o projeto, mas fez ressalvas quanto ao orçamento final.

examples.en_text: It is important that you express caveats if you don't agree with all the rules.
examples.target_text: É importante que você faça ressalvas se não concordar com todas as regras.

examples.en_text: She always made reservations before recommending a book to her friends.
examples.target_text: Ela sempre fazia ressalvas antes de recomendar um livro para os amigos.

examples.en_text: I would express caveats about this decision if I were in the meeting.
examples.target_text: Eu faria ressalvas sobre essa decisão se estivesse na reunião.

explanation_en: A euphemistic idiom where 'pê' stands for 'puto' (pissed off). It is used to express strong annoyance or anger in a slightly more polite or socially acceptable way than using the actual swear word.

examples.en_text: I always get pissed off when the bus is more than half an hour late.
examples.target_text: Eu sempre fico pê da vida quando o ônibus atrasa mais de meia hora.

examples.en_text: She got extremely annoyed because her brother took her car without asking.
examples.target_text: Ela ficou pê da vida porque o irmão pegou o carro dela sem pedir.

examples.en_text: We get really pissed off when the internet goes down in the middle of an important meeting.
examples.target_text: A gente fica pê da vida quando a internet cai no meio de uma reunião importante.

examples.en_text: My dad got extremely annoyed with the neighbors' noise in the middle of the night.
examples.target_text: Meu pai ficou pê da vida com o barulho dos vizinhos de madrugada.

examples.en_text: They get really pissed off when the company cancels the project without giving any explanations.
examples.target_text: Eles ficam pê da vida quando a empresa cancela o projeto sem dar explicações.

examples.en_text: Wouldn't you get extremely annoyed if you lost all your work on the computer?
examples.target_text: Você não ficaria pê da vida se perdesse todo o seu trabalho no computador?

explanation_en: A playful, highly informal Brazilian slang expression meaning 'crazy,' 'nuts,' or 'out of one's mind.' It is lighthearted and typically used to describe someone's bizarre behavior or irrationality without being overly offensive.

examples.en_text: With so much work piled up this week, I'm already going a bit crazy.
examples.target_text: Com tanto trabalho acumulado esta semana, eu já estou ficando meio lelê da cuca.

examples.en_text: My uncle is a bit crazy, but he has a heart of gold.
examples.target_text: O meu tio é um pouco lelê da cuca, mas ele tem um coração de ouro.

examples.en_text: Did you put the keys inside the fridge? Have you gone completely out of your mind?
examples.target_text: Você guardou as chaves dentro da geladeira? Ficou lelê da cuca de vez?

examples.en_text: If I don't sleep at least seven hours tonight, tomorrow I'm going to wake up totally out of my mind.
examples.target_text: Se eu não dormir pelo menos sete horas hoje, amanhã vou acordar totalmente lelê da cuca.

examples.en_text: That idea of traveling without planning anything seems like something from someone who is out of their mind.
examples.target_text: Aquela ideia de viajar sem planejar nada parece coisa de quem está lelê da cuca.

examples.en_text: This unbearable heat is driving everyone in the office a bit crazy.
examples.target_text: Esse calor insuportável está deixando todo mundo no escritório meio lelê da cuca.

explanation_en: This expression means to complete a process, project, or investigation without giving up. It is a very common collocation in both spoken and written Portuguese, often used in political, legal, or personal contexts. It emphasizes persistence and thoroughness.

examples.en_text: I started this project and I am going to carry it through to the end.
examples.target_text: Eu comecei este projeto e vou levá-lo até o final.

examples.en_text: Despite all the difficulties, we carried the work through to the end.
examples.target_text: Apesar de todas as dificuldades, nós levamos o trabalho até o final.

examples.en_text: If you accept this challenge, you need to carry it through to the end.
examples.target_text: Se você aceitar esse desafio, precisa levar até o final.

examples.en_text: Don't give up now, we have to carry this plan through to the end.
examples.target_text: Não desista agora, nós temos que levar este plano até o final.

examples.en_text: She is very dedicated and always carries her commitments through to the end.
examples.target_text: Ela é muito dedicada e sempre leva seus compromissos até o final.

examples.en_text: I would like to carry the Spanish course through to the end, but I don't have time.
examples.target_text: Eu gostaria de levar o curso de espanhol até o final, mas não tenho tempo.

explanation_en: This construction combines the verb 'ficar' with the gerund 'faltando' to indicate that something remains incomplete or is still needed. It is highly idiomatic and preferred in spoken Portuguese over simply saying 'falta'. It is useful for pointing out gaps in plans, lists, or investigations.

examples.en_text: We did the shopping for the cake, but the baking powder was left missing.
examples.target_text: Fizemos as compras para o bolo, mas ficou faltando o fermento.

examples.en_text: I finished the report, but signing the last page was left missing.
examples.target_text: Eu terminei o relatório, mas ficou faltando assinar a última página.

examples.en_text: You gave me twenty reais, so one real was still left missing to pay the bill.
examples.target_text: Você me deu vinte reais, então ainda ficou faltando um real para pagar a conta.

examples.en_text: I packed the whole suitcase, but I think putting in the phone charger was left missing.
examples.target_text: Arrumei a mala inteira, mas acho que ficou faltando colocar o carregador do celular.

examples.en_text: We presented almost the whole project, the only thing left missing was deciding on the final budget.
examples.target_text: Apresentamos quase todo o projeto, só ficou faltando decidir o orçamento final.

examples.en_text: The party decoration is beautiful, but putting on the background music was left missing.
examples.target_text: A decoração da festa está linda, mas ficou faltando colocar a música de fundo.

explanation_en: This is a very common formal collocation meaning to continue or sustain an ongoing project, action, or tradition. It is widely used in news, business, and political discourse instead of the simpler verb 'continuar'. It takes the preposition 'a' (or 'ao', 'à') to link to the object.

examples.en_text: We need to get more funding to continue this project.
examples.target_text: Precisamos de obter mais verba para dar continuidade a este projeto.

examples.en_text: After finishing her bachelor's degree, she wants to continue her studies abroad.
examples.target_text: Depois de terminar a licenciatura, ela quer dar continuidade aos estudos no estrangeiro.

examples.en_text: It is very important to follow through with the treatment, even if you already feel better.
examples.target_text: É muito importante dar continuidade ao tratamento, mesmo que já se sinta melhor.

examples.en_text: My brother decided to carry on the family business.
examples.target_text: O meu irmão decidiu dar continuidade ao negócio da família.

examples.en_text: We will continue the discussion in the next meeting.
examples.target_text: Nós daremos continuidade à discussão na próxima reunião.

examples.en_text: He started playing sports and hopes to keep up with that good habit.
examples.target_text: Ele começou a praticar desporto e espera dar continuidade a esse bom hábito.

explanation_en: This expression is used to express skepticism or uncertainty about a claim or a future outcome. While it translates directly to English, it is a crucial conversational tool in Portuguese for politely disagreeing or showing caution. It is often followed by 'se' (if) or 'que' (that).

examples.en_text: I have my doubts about whether this project will work out in the long run.
examples.target_text: Eu tenho minhas dúvidas se esse projeto vai dar certo a longo prazo.

examples.en_text: She says she is going to move countries next month, but I have my doubts.
examples.target_text: Ela diz que vai mudar de país no próximo mês, mas eu tenho minhas dúvidas.

examples.en_text: They want to have the wedding outdoors, but I have my doubts because of the rain.
examples.target_text: Eles querem fazer o casamento ao ar livre, mas tenho minhas dúvidas por causa da chuva.

examples.en_text: The salesman guaranteed that the phone is new, but I have my doubts.
examples.target_text: O vendedor garantiu que o celular é novo, mas eu tenho minhas dúvidas.

examples.en_text: He thinks he can learn to drive in a week, and I have my doubts.
examples.target_text: Ele acha que pode aprender a dirigir em uma semana, e eu tenho minhas dúvidas.

examples.en_text: If you think this is the best solution, fine, but I still have my doubts.
examples.target_text: Se você acha que essa é a melhor solução, tudo bem, mas eu ainda tenho minhas dúvidas.

explanation_en: This idiom refers to a very small, insignificant number of people attending an event where a larger crowd was expected. Literally translating to 'dripped cat,' it is highly colloquial and carries a slightly dismissive or mocking tone. It is always used in the plural ('uns gatos pingados') or singular to describe the crowd as a whole.

examples.en_text: We went to the rock concert, but only a handful of people showed up.
examples.target_text: Fomos ao concerto de rock, mas só apareceu meia dúzia de gatos pingados.

examples.en_text: The condo meeting was almost empty; there were only three or four scattered people there.
examples.target_text: A reunião de condomínio estava quase vazia; só lá estavam três ou quatro gatos pingados.

examples.en_text: With all this rain, the bar only had a few scattered people at the counter.
examples.target_text: Com esta chuva toda, o bar só tinha uns gatos pingados no balcão.

examples.en_text: They organized a protest in the square, but almost nobody went, just a handful of people.
examples.target_text: Eles organizaram um protesto na praça, mas não foi quase ninguém, só alguns gatos pingados.

examples.en_text: The teacher was disappointed because there was only a handful of people in the classroom.
examples.target_text: O professor ficou desapontado porque só havia meia dúzia de gatos pingados na sala de aula.

examples.en_text: The new store opened today, but only a few scattered people came in during the morning.
examples.target_text: A nova loja abriu hoje, mas só entraram uns gatos pingados durante a manhã.
